newsitem.title: USA: Johnson & Johnson's Nicotrol gets FDA OK.
newsitem.headline: Johnson & Johnson's Nicotrol gets FDA OK.

text.p: The United States Food and Drug Administration cleared the Nicotrol Inhaler nicotine inhalation system for prescription sale, McNeil Consumer Products Co said Monday.
McNeil is a unit of Johnson & Johnson.

The Inhaler is the first form of nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) to help control a smoker's cravings for cigarettes while satisfying the need for a key behavioral component of smoking, the hand-to-mouth ritual, which a smoker may repeat up to 73,000 times each year, McNeil said.

NRT provides nicotine, but at a lower level than cigarettes, so that smokers can alleviate their need for nicotine, McNeil said. And NRT does not contain the cancer-causing tars and toxins found within cigarettes and other tobacco products, McNeil said.
Currently available NRT products -- patch, gum, and nasal spray -- are designed to address physical cravings, McNeil said.

But many smokers also complain that they miss the cigarette and all the behaviors that go with it, like taking it out of the pack, lighting it, putting it to the lips, sucking, inhaling and holding it, NcNeil said.
The Inhaler is the only nicotine replacement therapy cleared by the FDA to provide the comfort of these smoking behaviors, McNeil said.
